nino-regions.alt: Overlapping Niño 4, Niño 3.4 and Niño 3 regions along the equator, with Niño 1+2 south of it near South America.
nino-regions.credit: Original ENSOLens diagram; geographic limits from NOAA CPC.
nino-regions.rights: ENSOLens original vector drawing; factual region coordinates from NOAA.

kelvin-wave.alt: A deeper thermocline disturbance moves east between two conceptual sections; it does not track one parcel of water.
kelvin-wave.credit: Original ENSOLens schematic; depth, distance and time are not to scale.
kelvin-wave.rights: ENSOLens original vector drawing; retained existing scientific explanation.

model-plume.alt: Three invented model-mean SST anomaly paths diverge from DJF to MAM; their dashed mean is not a probability.
model-plume.credit: Original ENSOLens teaching curves; invented values, not a current model forecast.
model-plume.rights: ENSOLens original vector drawing and hypothetical curves.

sierra-snow-level.alt: Conceptual Sierra cross-section shows rain below a moving storm snow level and snow storage above it.
sierra-snow-level.credit: Original ENSOLens conceptual elevation diagram; not a current snow-level forecast.

roni-ranges.alt: Nested DJF 2026–27 RONI intervals share one scale: central 90%, 70% and 50%, with median +2.28°C.
roni-ranges.credit: Original ENSOLens graphic of the preserved November 2026 CPC forecast; not local weather odds.
roni-ranges.rights: ENSOLens original rendering of NOAA CPC factual forecast values; source issue retained.

season-windows.alt: DJF, JFM, FMA, MAM and AMJ are overlapping three-month windows spanning December through June.
season-windows.credit: Original ENSOLens calendar diagram; calendar overlap alone does not classify an ENSO episode.
season-windows.rights: ENSOLens original vector drawing of calendar windows.

northwest-snow.alt: A skier descends a snow-covered mountain beside a forested slope near Yellow Pine, Idaho.
northwest-snow.credit: USDA Forest Service / Todd Leeds; location photo, not current snow conditions.
northwest-snow.rights: Existing USDA-hosted photo credited USDA Forest Service / Todd Leeds; federal employee work attribution, retained source credit. Recheck per-asset credit before reuse elsewhere.

winter-circulation.alt: NOAA schematic compares typical winter jet-stream patterns in La Niña and El Niño; it does not depict neutral.
winter-circulation.credit: NOAA / NWS event-phase comparison, not a neutral map or current winter forecast.
winter-circulation.rights: Existing NOAA/NWS government schematic; original attribution retained; no endorsement implied.

winter-temperature.alt: CPC temperature outlook issued November 19, 2026 for December 2026 through February 2027: warmth favored across the northern two-thirds of the contiguous U.S.; near-normal favored in parts of the Southeast; equal chances in parts of the Southwest.
winter-temperature.credit: NOAA CPC; original issue, validity dates, legend and map retained.
winter-temperature.rights: NOAA CPC government forecast map, retained unmodified with original dates/legend; no endorsement implied.

soi-ocean.alt: SOI uses standardized Tahiti–Darwin pressure contrast; Niño 3.4 uses regional sea-surface temperature. Their typical El Niño signs differ and their scales cannot be converted.
soi-ocean.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
soi-ocean.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
soi-ocean.caption: Original ENSOLens quantity comparison, not current readings. SOI is a standardized pressure contrast with provider-specific units; conventional Niño 3.4 is an SST departure in °C. Typical El Niño signs are not a conversion formula. Match provider, baseline and averaging window before comparing.

climate-timescales.alt: Separate conceptual curves show a rising long-term temperature background and oscillating ENSO variability; neither curve contains observations or a forecast.
climate-timescales.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
climate-timescales.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
climate-timescales.caption: Original ENSOLens conceptual curves, with no measured values, common time scale or forecast. Long-term background warming and ENSO variability answer different questions. The panels are not components to add together or an attribution of a particular storm. The IPCC assessment and its rainfall-versus-SST distinction remain in the text.

heatwave-enso.alt: A regional warm patch is contrasted with central and eastern equatorial Pacific warmth plus atmospheric evidence. Neither schematic shows a current marine heatwave or El Niño.
heatwave-enso.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
heatwave-enso.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
heatwave-enso.caption: Original ENSOLens spatial schematics, not maps of current conditions or geographic boundaries. A marine heatwave needs its own product’s location, duration and baseline criteria. El Niño assessment also needs atmospheric evidence. A regional warm patch can coexist with ENSO but does not establish the phase; the Blob-Class threshold in the table is not a universal heatwave definition.

water-stores.alt: Soil roots, mountain snow, a reservoir and a groundwater well illustrate four separate water stores requiring their own observations to assess drought recovery.
water-stores.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
water-stores.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
water-stores.caption: Original ENSOLens diagnostic cross-sections, not measured levels or recovery times. These are separate stores, not a required sequence in which rainfall refills them. Check root-zone moisture, basin SWE, reservoir storage and local well levels with their dates; operations, recharge and withdrawals also matter.

winter-pathway.alt: A qualitative boreal-winter pathway links tropical rainfall and heating to large-scale circulation, jet and storm-track tendencies, then local weather affected by elevation and air mass.
winter-pathway.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
winter-pathway.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
winter-pathway.caption: Original ENSOLens conceptual pathway for Northern Hemisphere winter, not a map of today’s jet stream. Arrows indicate influence, not guaranteed outcomes. Other climate patterns, storm position, elevation and air mass affect the local result; use local forecasts and warnings for a particular storm.

baseline-ruler.alt: On a shared 26 to 29°C scale, the same invented 28°C SST is 1°C above a 27°C reference and 0.5°C above a 27.5°C reference.
baseline-ruler.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
baseline-ruler.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
baseline-ruler.caption: Original ENSOLens invented arithmetic, not observations or RONI. Both panels share a 26–29°C scale and the same 28°C temperature. Only the reference changes: +1.0°C versus +0.5°C. Actual comparisons must also match season, region, dataset and processing.

observing-system.alt: Ocean instruments feed a processed SST analysis, regional and seasonal indices. Separately observed winds, pressure and rainfall also feed the ENSO assessment.
observing-system.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
observing-system.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
observing-system.caption: Original ENSOLens processing schematic. Product methods differ; not every analysis uses every observing platform. Regional averaging and seasonal processing do not turn SST into atmospheric observations. Winds, pressure and convection are assessed separately alongside the ocean evidence.

lifecycle-clocks.alt: A conceptual ocean-temperature peak, a combined ocean–atmosphere phase assessment and separate regional water and weather evidence answer different timing questions without supplying an end date.
lifecycle-clocks.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
lifecycle-clocks.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
lifecycle-clocks.caption: Original ENSOLens timing schematic, not a current forecast, timeline or measured curve. Peak temperature, operational phase and regional impacts need different evidence. The panels set no universal delay or ordering for impacts and no neutral-transition date. Use the dated CPC outlook below for actual target seasons.

product-windows.alt: Weekly conventional SST observations, overlapping three-month relative RONI windows and a monthly-issued three-category seasonal forecast are shown as distinct products.
product-windows.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
product-windows.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
product-windows.caption: Original ENSOLens product-reading schematic, not current values or probabilities. Weekly conventional SST, three-month relative RONI and monthly-issued seasonal probabilities have different constructions and dates. The calendar examples illustrate windows only; forecast categories are labels, not equal numerical odds. Source-specific methods and references are listed in the text.

three-phases.alt: El Niño has central and eastern equatorial Pacific warmth with an atmospheric response; La Niña has cooling with an atmospheric response; neutral is neither event and can include ocean–atmosphere mismatch.
three-phases.credit: Original ENSOLens explanatory diagram; conceptual, not current conditions.
three-phases.rights: ENSOLens original artwork; editable SVG and generator retained; scientific sources credited.
three-phases.caption: Original ENSOLens conceptual phase comparison based on NWS definitions, rechecked November 27, 2026 (source has no displayed publication date). Strips show qualitative central/eastern equatorial Pacific temperature departures, not observations, thresholds or jet-stream maps. Neutral is neither event; SST is often near average, but ocean and atmosphere can be out of step. None of the phases guarantees normal local weather.
